entry.content:
Fixes

Schemacraft Beta: Known Issues & Survey Preliminary Notice

November 26, 2026
Balance

Hello, this is Project Moon.

We would like to inform you of known issues identified in "Schemacraft Beta", updated Nov. 26th, 2026, and the schedule for the upcoming Schemacraft Beta survey.

Please refer below for more information.

<Known Issues>

▶ An issue where an Identity's action frequency may vary within the same shared turn depending on their Skill animation length

[Cause]
- While an Identity's Skill animation is playing, their action gauge for triggering their next action remains paused in the current version of Schemacraft.
- Because the sum of "Skill animation length" and "the time it takes for the action gauge to refill" determines the interval between an Identity's actions, Identities with shorter Skill animations are more likely to take an additional action within the same shared turn.
- Despite not being displayed on each Identity's information page, Skill animation length was affecting the Identities' action economy.

[Affected Areas]
- All units, both allies and enemies, are guaranteed at least 1 action per shared turn. Units with fast Speed values may even take 2 or more actions per shared turn.
- This animation length issue comes into play when an Identity takes, or plans to take, a second action within the same shared turn.
- The ability to take an extra action has a direct effect on an Identity's damage output and status application, which affects balancing.
※ However, as Skills with multiple Coins generally deal more damage in a single action, the action economy isn't the sole determinant of an Identity's power.

[Improvement Direction: Combat Action Economy Adjustments]
We are planning to move the next action preparation trigger from "After the Skill animation is completed" to "After a certain amount of time has passed since the Skill animation began".
Through this, we can remove animation length from the equation, making it so that action economy is determined only by a verifiable factor, the Speed value.
※ If an Identity has a short animation, it will generally wait for a period of time from the start of its animation before the next action is prepared.
※ The time loss due to long animations will be factored into calculating how long it takes for an Identity to prepare their next action.

If an Identity has a long animation, the next action will generally start preparing before the animation ends.

1. Changes to Gameplay Feel
(1) You may notice Identities on standby after using Skills with brief animations.
(2) Identities who have longer animations will now take their next action earlier than they used to.
(3) Shorter animations will have less effect on the action economy, and Identities with faster Speed values will now have a clearer advantage.

※ The length and tempo of each Encounter will generally remain the same.
※ You may notice the above (1) ~ (3) changes on enemy units as well.

2. What Remains the Same
(1) Using an E.G.O will not delay the Identity's next action.
(2) Defense Skills that ended without receiving an attack will not be subject to waiting periods.

<Upcoming Schemacraft Beta Survey>

We will be conducting a survey to gather feedback from our Managers on their experiences with the Schemacraft Beta. Through this survey, we will identify possible areas and directions for improvement.

- Survey Date: Dec. 3rd (Thu), 2026 (KST)

We will inform you again via a separate notice when the survey is released.

We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience.
Thank you.

entry.title: New Content - Schemacraft Beta
entry.summary: With the Nov. 26th, 2026 (KST) Scheduled Update, new content ["Schemacraft Beta"] will be added to the game. Covers Gameplay, Content Progression, Combat Progression, and 2 more topics.
entry.content:
Announcements

New Content - Schemacraft Beta

November 24, 2026
Main StoryNew ContentRewards

Greetings, Dear Manager.

With the Nov. 26th, 2026 (KST) Scheduled Update, new content ["Schemacraft Beta"] will be added to the game.

▶ Unlock Conditions Clear all Stages of Chapter 9.5 "Mnestic Experience" and Chapter 10 "The Gaze Bearing"

Description

- With the Nov. 26th Scheduled Update, the "Schemacraft" button on the Drive tab will be activated.

- You may earn Schemacraft Pass EXP based on your progress through each run in Schemacraft Beta.

- "Schemacraft Beta" does not cost any Enkephalin or Enkephalin Modules to play.

※ Playing through "Schemacraft" will not raise your Limbus Pass levels or EXP. Activities within Schemacraft will not count toward clearing Limbus Pass Missions either.

※ The version of "Schemacraft" to be updated on Nov. 26th will be in a playable Beta form and will be consistently adjusted and improved following the initial update.

※ All images featured in this notice are for demonstration purposes only. Final content after the update may look different.

Gameplay

▶ Schemacraft Beta
- Clear all Stages of Chapter 9.5 "Mnestic Experience" and Chapter 10 "The Gaze Bearing" to unlock "Schemacraft Beta".

- Progress through the nodes, recruit Identities and E.G.O, and fight your way through its Encounters using its new auto-battle feature.

- Gain Exclusive Pass EXP based on your Schemacraft progress and earn various rewards by raising the Pass level.

- Once a run has started, select "Pause and Exit" to leave the gameplay mode. You can then choose to either continue that run with the same deck or restart with a new Team.

※ In "Schemacraft" mode, Identities and E.G.O Uptie/Threadspin tiers vary depending on whether you have acquired them outside the mode.

- Identities
Owned: Can upgrade up to Uptie 4
Not Owned: Can upgrade up to Uptie 3
- E.G.O
Owned: Applies your current Threadspin Tier
Not Owned: Applies Threadspin Tier 1

※ Unobtained COLLABORATION - LIMITED E.G.O will not appear.

- Relevant E.G.O → Command : Meltdown Faust, To Remain Oneself [TEE] Hong Lu, Tidal Elegy Ishmael, Unbrilliant Glory Gregor

Content Progression

▶ Starting Team
- Spend the starting Cost to select up to 4 Sinners and their Identities as your Starting Team.

- Starting Cost for Manual Team is 6 Cost; for Randomized Team, 10.

- Should you select the "Reshuffle Randomized Team" option, other previously randomized Teams will be listed under the "Randomized Teams" section.

※ Per-ldentity Cost varies based on each Identity's release date and rarity.

※ Randomized Teams will automatically equip the Identities within the starting Cost budget of 10, which is 4 higher than starting as a Manual Team.

※ Randomized Teams will obtain +40% more Schemacraft Pass EXP.

※ You may Reshuffle your starting Randomized Team 3 times between each daily reset. Certain progress milestone options in each completed Schemacraft run may recharge the Reshuffle function. The total number of Reshuffles, however, cannot exceed 3.
※ While Identities you do not own can be equipped, they may only be upgraded to Tier 3 within the gameplay mode.

▶ How to Progress
- Movement between rooms in "Schemacraft" is determined by a dice roll. Each room may contain combat Encounters or Respites.

- The dice rolls from a range of 1~3, and the resulting number decides the upper limit of how many nodes (called Representations) you may travel.

- Each roll of the dice after the 5th roll in each Schema zone will give empowering effects to the enemies, called "Schema Deformation".

▶ Combat Information
- Before each battle, you may preview the list of possible Pack rewards and the average level of featured enemies.

- The Pack list is chosen at random. The name of each reward Pack indicates the relevant Keyword, faction, or Sinner for the Identities it features.

※ While Elite Encounter Representations yield better rewards than Regular Encounters, their featured enemies will receive certain empowering effects.

▶ Entering Representations
- You may rearrange your Team's Deployment Order prior to entering each Encounter.

- Initially, Combat Encounters in "Schemacraft" will only feature 4 allied Identities. As you progress through each Schemacraft run, however, your team will slowly expand up to 8 fielded Identities at once, with 4 Backup Units.

- You cannot begin an Encounter unless you have set Deployment Orders for all Sinners in your roster.

- In "Schemacraft", the Sinners' SP values carry over between Encounters.

- Sinners defeated in an Encounter enter the next at 0 SP.

- Backup Identities receive bonus SP upon entry, with a baseline of positive modifiers.

※ Identities who exclusively use Minus Coins, however, will receive negative SP modifiers upon Substitution. (Lobotomy E.G.O::Sunshower Heathcliff, The One Who Shall Grip Sinclair)
※ Identities whose Coin types change based on their SP will receive appropriate SP modifiers for their SP value upon Substitution. (Lobotomy E.G.O::In the Name of Love and Hate Don Quixote, Lobotomy E.G.O::The Sword Sharpened with Tears Rodion)

▶ Defense Strategy
- Configure how each Identity uses Defense Skills.

- During combat, Identities automatically use Defense Skills according to their individual settings.

- Each Identity follows the Default setting unless changed.

- Use "Set All to Default," "Apply Selected Identity's Settings to All," or "No One Defends" at the bottom of the screen to update every Sinner's Defense Strategy at once.

▶ Briefing
- Review ally and enemy information, including each side's average level, before starting a battle.

- Enemy information includes the number of initial enemies and reinforcements, along with their levels and weaknesses.

- The total resources required to use E.G.O are shown alongside the amount of resources Identities can generate.

Combat Progression

▶ Combat Progression
- In "Schemacraft," Combat Progression is automated.

- Each ally and enemy acts in an order determined by its Speed range. Units use Attack Skills from their Skill stash to Clash or make Unopposed Attacks, and use Defense Skills according to their Defense Strategy.

- A shared turn ends once every ally and enemy has acted at least once. Faster units may act multiple times within a single turn.

- All effects on allies and enemies follow this shared turn count.

※ Use the Show/Hide UI button in the upper-right corner to toggle the battle interface.

※ E.G.O resources do not carry over between battles. Instead, at the start of each battle, you gain (number of Attack Skills in the Sin Affinity / 2) E.G.O resources for each respective Affinity, rounded down. This counts from all Identities in your Team, including Backup Units.

※ Sapling of Light abilities cannot be used in Schemacraft battles.

▶ Using E.G.O
- Once the required resources are available, you can use E.G.O at any time to help turn the battle in your team's favor.

- Click or tap an E.G.O icon to queue it for activation. Its target is selected automatically.

- Click or tap a queued E.G.O icon again to cancel its use.

- Drag an E.G.O icon onto an enemy on the battlefield to target that enemy.

- Drag an E.G.O icon downward to Overclock it.

- You can retry or forfeit a stage during battle.

※ Each battle allows up to 2 retries.

※ Forfeiting a stage also consumes 1 retry. Losing or forfeiting with no retries remaining ends the Schemacraft run.

▶ Battle Report
- Review a detailed report after each battle.

Battle Rewards

▶ Choosing a Reward Pack
- After winning a battle, choose a Reward Pack from those available at that Representation.

- Reward Packs can offer Identities associated with their featured keyword, faction, or Sinner, with at least 1 matching Identity guaranteed.

- If none of the offered Packs are suitable, spend a Reshuffle to replace 1 Reward Pack with another from the remaining pool.

- Clearing Elite and Boss Representations in each Schema zone grants slightly better rewards than clearing Regular Encounter Representations.

▶ Regular Encounter Representation
- Selecting a Reward Pack reveals a list of Identities and E.G.O. Select the indicated number of rewards from this list.

- Spend a Reshuffle attempt to refresh the offered Identities and E.G.O once.

- Team → Recruit the Identity to the current team. If that Sinner is already on the team, replace their current Identity. Obtaining a duplicate Identity raises its current Uptie Tier by 1 or sets it to the Uptie Tier shown on the reward, whichever is higher.
- Sliver → Convert the reward into 1-3 Slivers for that Sinner, based on the reward's displayed Uptie Tier, instead of adding or replacing an Identity. If that Sinner has already reached the Uptie Tier cap, receive Universal Slivers instead. You can use Universal Slivers at Rest Nodes.
- E.G.O rewards are equipped in the corresponding E.G.O Risk Level-based Slot of a Sinner on the team. If that Sinner is absent, the E.G.O is stored. Selecting another E.G.O of the same Risk Level allows the existing E.G.O to be replaced.

※ If adding a Sinner would exceed the team limit, one of the Sinners already on the team can be replaced.

※ When replacing an Identity, the new Identity uses the Uptie Tier shown on its reward, and some of that Sinner's Slivers are refunded.

※ Unowned Identities and E.G.O can also appear. The following rules apply when using them.
- Identities can only be upgraded to Uptie Tier III within Schemacraft.
- E.G.O is equipped at Threadspin Tier I.

※ Unobtained COLLABORATION - LIMITED E.G.O will not appear.

- Relevant E.G.O → Command : Meltdown Faust, To Remain Oneself [TEE] Hong Lu, Tidal Elegy Ishmael, Unbrilliant Glory Gregor

▶ Elite Encounter Representation
- Winning an Elite Encounter grants an Elite Reward.
- Replace Identity: Replace a specified Sinner's Identity with another Identity.
- Recruit Identity: Add a specified Identity to the team.
- Upgrade: Obtain 3 Slivers for a Sinner currently on the team, which may increase their Uptie Tier.

※ When choosing Replace Identity or Recruit Identity, if that Sinner already has an Identity in the team, Slivers are granted based on the previous Identity's Uptie Tier.

▶ Boss Encounter Representation
- After winning a Boss Encounter, choose between 2 reward options, which may offer Reshuffles, Identity Uptie Tier increases, or Universal Slivers.

- Each reward option also includes an additional choice of a Sinner Pack or a Random Pack.

※ The available Boss Encounter reward options may vary by Schema.

- Obtain specific Identities and E.G.O at the cost of 0~2 remaining dice rolls, depending on the option selected.

- If there are not enough dice rolls remaining, the "Deformation" effect is applied instead.

▶ Event Representation
- Choose beneficial effects to aid in battle, along with drawbacks that strengthen enemies.

- After clearing Schemacraft through the boss of Schema 5 once, additional Event Representations with special choices will become available.

※ If too many drawbacks have accumulated or none of the benefits are worthwhile, passing without making a selection can be a sound strategy.

▶ Respite Representation
- Choose 1 of 3 options at a Respite Representation. Universal Slivers obtained from Reward Packs can also be spent here.
- Reshuffles + → Gain additional reshuffles for Reward Packs, Identities, and E.G.O.
- Uptie Tier + for 1 Identity → Increase the Uptie Tier of 1 Identity in the team.
- Bonus Rolls + → Gain additional dice rolls for movement. This bonus carries over when advancing to the next Schema.
- Spend Universal Slivers to increase the Uptie Tier of an Identity of choice.

※ When Uptying, Identities not obtained by your account may only be Uptied to Tier 3.

※ Uptie Tiers available at each Respite Representation in each Schema are as follows (same applies when Uptying via Universal Slivers):

- Schema 1 ~ Schema 3: Up to Uptie 3
- Schema 4 ~ Schema 5: Up to Uptie 4

Final Results & Schemacraft Pass

▶ Final Battle Results
- There are 3 ways to end a Schemacraft Run and view your Final Battle Results: 1) Clear the final boss on "Schema 5";
2) Lose an Encounter with 0 Retries remaining;
3) Selecting "Forfeit Schemacraft Run" in the options menu.

- On this screen, you may review various details of your progress, such as Identities used, damage tally, Schemacraft EXP gained, and more.

▶ Schemacraft Pass
- Gain Schemacraft Pass EXP based on the Encounter outcomes.

- Higher Schemacraft zones and difficult Encounters will yield more Schemacraft Pass EXP.

- Beginning with a Randomized Team will yield a +40% bonus on Schemacraft Pass EXP.

※ Up to 1,000 Schemacraft Pass EXP may be gained per week. This cap will be reset every Thursday, 06:00 (KST).

※ Schemacraft Pass EXP cannot be gained past the currently unlocked Pass level.

※ Obtain "Nominable Announcer Ticket [Yisang Exchange] (Schemacraft Beta)" as a special reward upon reaching Schemacraft Pass Level 10.
- Use this item to select and obtain an Announcer from a limited list of Announcers that can be acquired through Yisang Exchange on the Extraction menu. (※ Only Announcers released up to the Season 8's end date can be obtained through this item. Does not include Walpurgis Night Announcers.)

BalanceMain Story

The server will enter scheduled maintenance from 10:00 AM through 12:00 PM on November 19th, 2026 (KST).

Please make note of the maintenance schedule; we recommend that you refrain from entering combat or making in-app purchases and close the application before maintenance begins so that no data is lost.

Please refer to the details below for the update.

Major Changes

1. Improved Text on the Unit Details Synergy Tab

※ The improved animation will differ from the one shown in the PV.

entry.title: The 10th Walpurgis Night Identity Enhancement and Apology on Encounter Design
entry.summary: Adds the 10th Walpurgis Night Identity Enhancement and Apology on Encounter Design. Explains its encounters and E.G.O Gifts.
entry.content:
Announcements

The 10th Walpurgis Night Identity Enhancement and Apology on Encounter Design

November 12, 2026
Identities & E.G.OEventsBalanceRewards

Hello, this is Kim Jihoon, Director of Project Moon.

We have confirmed that the performance and play experience of the Identities released for this Walpurgis Night have fallen short of our Managers' expectations.

After reviewing our design process, I found that our approach was flawed. We did not give enough thought to how reliably these Identities could use their key Skills in actual combat, or whether meeting the conditions for those Skills would feel rewarding. We also lacked a consistent standard for designing their performance. I apologize for disappointing the Managers who had been looking forward to their release.

Accordingly, we plan to increase the performance of certain buffs and Skills for the Outis, Don Quixote, and Sinclair Identities released for this Walpurgis Night, and adjust the Walpurgis Night Combat Encounter and E.G.O Gifts.

1. Identity Adjustments

1) Wedge Office Fixer Don Quixote
- Added an effect to "Field Analysis":
Turn Start: If this unit is Staggered, recover from Stagger (2 times per Encounter; excluding forced Staggers)

- Changed the Coin 3 effect of "My Spear Shall Puncture Thee True!":
Before: [On Hit] Deal Pierce damage equal to (Wedge - Sinclair on target x 5)% of this Coin's final damage (max 40%)
After: [On Hit] Deal Pierce damage equal to (Wedge - Sinclair on target x 7)% of this Coin's final damage (max 56%)

2) Wedge Office Fixer Sinclair
- Added an effect to "Field Analysis":
Turn Start: If this unit is Staggered, recover from Stagger (2 times per Encounter; excluding forced Staggers)

- Changed the Coin 3 effect of "I'll Run You Through Quick & True":
Before: [Reuse - On Hit] Deal Pierce damage equal to (Wedge - Don Quixote on target x 4)% of this Coin's final damage (max 32%)
After:  [Reuse - On Hit] Deal Pierce damage equal to (Wedge - Don Quixote on target x 6)% of this Coin's final damage (max 48%)

3) Wedge Office Rep Outis
- Added an effect to "Momentum":
Turn Start: If this unit is Staggered, recover from Stagger (once per Encounter; excluding forced Staggers)

- Added a Coin 1 effect to "Transpierce":
[On Hit] Deal Pierce damage equal to 100% of this Coin's final damage

- Changed a Skill effect of "... All units, engage for collision.":
Before: [On Use] Deal +30% damage for every excess Atk Weight beyond the # of actual targets
After: [On Use] Deal +60% damage for every excess Atk Weight beyond the # of actual targets

- Added the following effect to Coins 1, 2, and 3 of "... All units, engage for collision.":
[On Hit] Deal Pierce damage equal to 15% of this Coin's final damage

- Changed a Skill effect of "The Wedge in the Wake of Dawnbreak":
Before: [On Use] Deal +30% damage for every excess Atk Weight beyond the # of actual targets
After: [On Use] Deal +60% damage for every excess Atk Weight beyond the # of actual targets

- Added the following effect to Coins 1, 2, and 3 of "The Wedge in the Wake of Dawnbreak":
[On Hit] Deal Pierce damage equal to 20% of this Coin's final damage

2. The 10th Walpurgis Night Combat Adjustment
- Added an effect that reduces damage taken from Burn by 75% to the Emotion Level 0, 1, 2, and 3 buffs

3. The 10th Walpurgis Night E.G.O Gift Keyword Adjustments
- White Cravat
Before: Keywordless
After: Pierce

- Carefully-selected Medicinal Herbs
Before: Keywordless
After: Pierce

Before deploying the adjustments, I would like to explain how this happened and why I believe these Identities need upward adjustments. I would like to disclose the process as transparently as possible to our Managers, as unexplained changes could seem as though we were judging the design and balance solely by monitoring player reactions.

In reviewing the situation, I identified four major problems:

[1. Combo Skill Performance]

The Wedge Office Identities were designed around using their "Combo" Skills.
However, despite needing all 5 Identities and their respective conditions, the 5-Identity combo Skill damage output was in the same ballpark as the other newest Identities' powerful Skills.

In our original design process, we decided to give the combo Attack a relatively low damage output. It was because we decided that the combined total damage output of Wedge Office's attack cycle, when taking into account the additional attacks from combo Skills, was sufficiently high.

However, in this process, we failed to consider the actual gameplay experience of building up a powerful combo attack.
We should have considered it from the Managers' point of view: a key Skill that requires several conditions and plays out through a lengthy animation should deliver power and satisfaction to match. We featured the Joint Combo prominently in the PV, and we should have considered what Managers would expect from it.

We believe that, even if the total damage is high enough, disappointing damage output for the most anticipated move in the Skillset dampens the primary fun factor of using the Identity in question. It was our mistake to weaken the core Skill's damage for the sake of balancing the total damage output.

Going forward, when balancing an Identity, we will review whether an Identity's core concept and Skills provide enough power and satisfaction as our first priority, instead of reviewing based on the final, total damage output.

[2. Reliability Issue]

Due to the inconsistent reliability of Wedge Office Identities, their combo moves were too infrequently activated despite being their core mechanic.

Don Quixote and Sinclair each have 2 Stagger Thresholds, and none of the Wedge Office Identities had any ability to recover from Stagger.
They also lacked any means to alleviate that issue, such as healing, which meant that Identities that were supposed to participate in combo attacks were unable to do so due to Stagger. This led to combo attacks and joint moves being executed less frequently than most would hope for.

Though the Dawn Office Identities also lack any Stagger recovery ability, they have self-healing, which ensures a degree of survivability.
This is something we failed to consider when designing the Wedge Office Identities.
As these Identities and their actions were designed to work in conjunction with each other, we should have prepared the means to reliably sustain that design structure.

Another reason behind this design is the lack of consistency in translating lore into Identity strength.
In this case, we did not give Wedge Office Stagger recovery because we considered the original Dawn Office and original Wedge Office's strengths to be, in terms of lore, on relatively similar levels.

However, in other parts of the design process, we gave them abilities different from the original versions because they were Mirror World Identities. Examples include Wedge Office's Joint Combo attacks or Burn infliction from Dawn Office's Yuna.
This lack of worldbuilding-and-gameplay consistency caused us to miss an important part of the gameplay design.

In addition, as we have been including various utilities such as Stagger recovery, Shield, or healing in recent, powerful Identities, we should have considered whether these new Identities had the same level of reliability and utilities.
We failed to sufficiently review and provide the Identity strength and satisfying gameplay feel that the newest Walpurgis Night Identities should have.

Going forward, we will establish a more concrete set of standards for incorporating worldbuilding details into actual combat gameplay experiences.
Also, we will more carefully review whether an Identity's core mechanic can be reliably engaged with in a real gameplay scenario.

[3. Using the Identities in the Walpurgis Night Combat Encounter]

Enemies in this Walpurgis Night Combat Encounter primarily use the Burn debuff, but the Wedge Office Identities had no particular means of dealing with it.

We should have considered that Managers would want to use the Identities they had just obtained through Extraction in the new Combat Encounter released alongside them. Because we failed to take this into account, the Wedge Office Identities could not perform well in the Walpurgis event battle.

Their difficulty dealing with Burn, combined with their lack of survivability, made the Joint Combo Skills even harder to use. Even when players managed to use it, its damage fell short of expectations. This made their performance and play experience all the more disappointing.

A Walpurgis Night Combat Encounter released alongside new Identities should have been a stage where those Identities could be used properly and showcase their strength.

Game design work for the Identities, E.G.O, and Combat Encounter was divided too sharply between teams, and we did not sufficiently review how the aforementioned elements worked together. The design team lead and I should have ensured that the people-in-charge continued to share information and coordinate their work. We failed to do that, and as a result, we overlooked the Managers' experience of playing the content.

Going forward, the design team will review together whether simultaneously-released Identities and E.G.O can fulfill their intended roles in the accompanying Combat Encounter.

[4. Keywordless E.G.O Gifts Issue]

In the current Mirror Dungeon, it is difficult to obtain a specific E.G.O Gift classified as Keywordless. Nevertheless, all three E.G.O Gifts added for this Walpurgis Night were classified as Keywordless.

To put it plainly, I am deeply sorry: we made that decision without thinking it through. We classified the Gifts as Keywordless because there was no Keyword that clearly matched their effects, without sufficiently considering how that classification would affect players' ability to obtain them. I apologize for overlooking such a basic point that should have been considered before all else.

In the current Mirror Dungeon, a Keywordless classification does more than describe the nature of a Gift. It also makes that Gift difficult to obtain deliberately.

We should therefore have considered whether the Gift offered enough in return for that difficulty, and whether the classification placed needless restrictions on the way players could use it. If there was no design-related reason to make a Gift harder to obtain, we could have assigned it a suitable Keyword such as Pierce. Instead, we classified it as Keywordless simply because no Keyword matched its functions exactly.

This was an issue that a little more thought could have prevented. It made me recognize, once again, that something was wrong with how the design team communicated during the process. And once again, I deeply apologize for this oversight.

Going forward, we will review not only the E.G.O Gifts' effects, but also how their Keyword classification affects how they can be obtained and how difficult they are to obtain.

[5. Our Next Steps]

I apologize again for these design errors in the 10th Walpurgis Night. I recognize it is an important event that should have been enjoyable for all Managers.

First, I intend to examine whether the current Walpurgis Night schedule placed an unreasonable workload on the design team and those in charge.
Afterward, I will review how work is assigned and what standards should guide the resulting designs.
I will also spend more time asking our game designers what they intended and what considerations informed their decisions.
The design team lead and I will speak with team members more often, so that no employee is left focused only on their assigned portion of the work.

I feel particularly sorry and ashamed because we could have avoided these problems by playing Limbus Company in-depth, in-house, and giving the designs a little more thought.

I believe this is a systemic problem in our design and implementation process, rather than a matter of isolated human error. I will consider how that process needs to change.

[6. How We Review Player Feedback]

I would also like to explain how we review reactions to updates, as some Managers may be concerned that we make patch decisions based only on responses from a particular language group or online community.

In the past, I could only review feedback from Korean-language communities. Even then, time constraints sometimes prevented me from seeing all of it.

To overcome these language and time constraints and hear from as many communities as possible, our internal Customer Support team uses monitoring tools to collect and organize opinions and reactions from major social media platforms across different language groups. The people in charge then review the collected feedback directly to perceive, analyze, and understand the overall response.

After major updates, we check this feedback at 1-hour intervals. At other times, we continue monitoring at intervals of 3 to 4 hours.

My own judgment will inevitably play a part in interpreting what we collect. Even so, I want Managers to know we are making an effort not to decide a patch's direction based on a single language group or community.

I apologize again that these issues arose during the Walpurgis Night event, especially with Project Moon's 10th Anniversary just around the corner. I understand that Managers have been looking forward to both of these events.

Because this is a serious matter, we will make the adjustments as quickly as possible through an update that does not require a new client build. We currently expect the hotfix to be deployed at approximately 11:00 PM (KST). We will issue another notice once the update is complete.

[Compensation for the 10th Walpurgis Night Identity Enhancement and Battle Design]

- Content: Lunacy x1300
- Recipients: All users whose game accounts were created before Nov. 26th, 2026, 10:00 AM (KST)
- When: After Nov. 12th (Thu), 2026, 23:00 (KST)
- Can be claimed once per account

Relevant Compensation can be claimed until Nov. 26th (Thu), 2026, 10:00 (KST) via the in-game Mailbox (mail available for 7 days).

Notice: Additional Issues To Be Fixed in the Nov. 12th Scheduled Update

November 11, 2026

Hello, this is Project Moon.

We would like to inform you of additional issues that will be fixed in the Scheduled Update on Nov. 12th (Thu) at 12:00 (KST).

Please refer below for details.

< Additional Issues To Be Fixed in the Scheduled Update >

▶ Fixed an issue where a certain Identity was not counted toward a "Mirror Projection / Achievements - Teams (Loadout)" achievement
→ Relevant Achievement: Clear Mirror Dungeon at Floor 5 or higher with 6 or more Office or Workshop Identities in your Loadout at the time of completion (Incompletable by Rental Teams)
- Before: "Jeong's Office Rep Ishmael" was not counted toward this achievement
- After: "Jeong's Office Rep Ishmael" will be counted toward this achievement

▶ Fixed an issue where EXP awarded after combat was distributed differently than intended when "Gregor's Support Identity" was assigned
- Before: Gregor's Support Identity was included in EXP distribution. If deployed in combat, it also received additional combat participation EXP.
- After: As with other Support Identities, no EXP will be distributed to Gregor's Identity while his Support Identity is assigned.

[Design Intent]

EXP earned from a Combat Encounter is distributed among the Sinners. Sinners assigned as Deployed Identities and Backup Identities receive slightly more EXP than those not assigned.

A Support Identity is not intended to receive EXP. Instead, the other 11 Sinners share the EXP.

[Identified Issue]

When Gregor's Support Identity was assigned, Gregor was still included in EXP distribution, so the EXP was shared among all 12 Sinners.

We also found that when Gregor's Support Identity was deployed in combat (as either a combat participant or a Backup Unit), the Gregor Identity equipped before the Support Identity was assigned received additional combat participation EXP, separate from the EXP awarded to the other Sinners.

[Examples of the Issue]

※ The following examples assume a total of 600 EXP earned from a battle with 6 participants. The other 6 Sinners are not deployed as either combat participant or Backup Unit. Decimal values are rounded down.

(1) No Support Identity used
6 combat participants = 59 EXP each
6 non-deployed Sinners = 41 EXP each

(2) Another Sinner's Support Identity assigned and deployed
5 combat participants = 66 EXP each
6 non-deployed Sinners = 45 EXP each Support Identity = 0 EXP

(3) Gregor's Support Identity assigned but not selected to be either a participant or a Backup Unit
6 combat participants = 59 EXP each
5 non-deployed Sinners = 41 EXP each Gregor's Identity = 41 EXP

(4) Gregor's Support Identity assigned and deployed
5 combat participants = 61 EXP each
6 non-deployed Sinners = 42 EXP each Gregor's Identity = 61 EXP

In examples (3) and (4), the EXP awarded to Gregor went to the Manager's Gregor Identity that had been equipped before his Support Identity was assigned. If that Identity was at the maximum level, EXP Tickets were awarded instead.

We also confirmed an issue where assigning Gregor's Support Identity and deploying it as either a Backup Unit or combat participant caused a greater amount of EXP than normal to be awarded.

[Fix]

After the Nov. 12th update, assigning Gregor's Support Identity will no longer award EXP to Gregor's Identity. As with other Support Identities, the remaining Sinners will share the EXP.

[Examples After the Fix]

※ The following examples assume a total of 600 EXP earned from a battle with 6 participants. The other 6 Sinners are not deployed as either combat participants or Backup Units. Decimal values are rounded down.

(1) No Support Identity used
6 combat participants = 59 EXP each
6 non-deployed Sinners = 41 EXP each

(2) Support Identity used, including Gregor's
5 combat participants = 66 EXP each
6 non-deployed Sinners = 45 EXP each Support Identity = 0 EXP

EXP and EXP Tickets obtained through this issue before the update will not be withdrawn from the Manager's account. Please note that the EXP currencies that have already been given will remain in the account.

We apologize for the confusion caused by identifying this issue so long after the feature was introduced. We will take greater care to prevent similar issues in the future.

entry.content:
Announcements

Apology & Next Steps on Yi Sang and Don Quixote's JP Translation Changes

November 9, 2026
Balance

Hello, this is Project Moon.

We would like to apologize for the changes to Yi Sang's and Don Quixote's speech in the Japanese translation introduced with the Oct. 29th (KST) update, and explain how we will address them.

On Oct. 29th, we revised the Japanese lines for the following characters to improve readability for the Managers.

1) Yi Sang
Yi Sang's Japanese dialogue contained elements of classical grammar that we felt made some lines difficult to follow. As a result, in recent chapters, we had instead expressed his voice through literary phrasing that incorporated Korean words and expressions. In the Oct. 29th update, we also revised his dialogue from the early story to match that style.

2) Don Quixote
For Don Quixote, we used archaic sentence endings to convey her knightly manner of speaking. However, some of those endings could have come across as a parody of a samurai's speech, which led to the recent revision.

These changes led to broader adjustments to both characters' voices, but we did not clearly explain them in the patch notes before making them. We failed to anticipate how confusing an unannounced change to familiar voices would be, and we realize that we should have considered the impact of the revisions more carefully.

Consequently, we will revert the changes to Yi Sang's and Don Quixote's speech with this update. Corrections to mistranslations that do not affect their manner of speech will be retained.

[Application Time]
After Nov. 12th, 12:00 (KST)

We apologize for the confusion and inconvenience caused by the sudden changes to these elements. During the revision process, we failed to pay enough attention to the characters' distinct voices or the Managers' experience of them.

Going forward, before making further improvements to the Japanese text, we will take the time to reassess our approach so that each character's distinct voice and personality are preserved in revisions. If a future revision is expected to substantially change how characters express themselves, we will explain the reasons for the change in detailed patch notes before deploying it.
We will continue to endeavor to deliver our textual changes in a more prudent and transparent manner.

Fixes to the "Judgment!" Skill of Haute Couture::Le Noir Brand Manager Don Quixote

We have identified implementation and text errors concerning the "Judgment!" Skill-related effects in the Passive "The Lord's Will and Values Be With Us..." and plan to fix them.

We apologize for having to announce multiple corrections to an Identity so soon after its release. We will take greater care to prevent similar issues.

Please refer below for details.

[Identified Issues]

The effect concerned was designed so that Don Quixote would perform an Unopposed Attack with the "Judgment!" Skill "before another allied Le Noir Identity used an Attack Skill or Counter Skill against an enemy". However, we identified the following issues:

1. The in-game text says "Before Attack" rather than "Before Use", which is the actual activation timing

2. The activation check is based only on Attack Skills assigned during the Chaining Phase. As a result, the effect does not activate for Skills used through Assist Attacks, Passive effects, or other means

3. The effect does not activate before Counter Skills, Clashable Counter Skills, or Attack Skills converted from Defense Skills at Combat Start

4. The Passive can activate even when the allied Le Noir Identity is unable to act and cannot use its Skill

[Cause of the Issue]

The effect was initially designed to activate only before the use of an Attack Skill. However, during testing, we decided to expand it to activate before the use of Counter Skills and Attack Skills converted from Defense Skills as well. While revising the description to cover these additional conditionals, we used the ambiguous phrase "Before Attack" —a different point in the attack sequence from "Before Use", which is the current activation timing. In addition, the expanded scope was not reflected in the in-game implementation. The activation check also remained based solely on Skills assigned during the Chaining Phase. Our review process did not catch these discrepancies between the intended design, implementation, and text.

[Fix Direction]

"Before Use" occurs before a Clash. "Before Attack" occurs after the Clash has ended, just before the attack itself begins.

Changing the effect's activation timing to match the current "Before Attack" text could cause the following issues:
1. Allies could no longer use the Tremor inflicted by "Judgment!" as a conditional to satisfy Power increase conditions.
2. "Judgment!" would not activate if an ally lost the Clash and could not attack.
3. "Judgment!" could no longer Stagger an enemy before the ally's Clash.

In short, changing the effect to match the current text in all cases could weaken the Identity. We will therefore retain the existing ""Before Use" activation timing and correct the missing activation cases and incorrect conditions.

[Scheduled Changes]

1. The Passive will activate before an allied Le Noir Identity uses a Counter Skill, Clashable Counter Skill, or Attack Skill converted from a Defense Skill at Combat Start.

2. The Passive's activation will be checked against the Skill an ally actually uses, rather than only the Skill assigned during the Chaining Phase.
- This will allow the effect to activate when another allied Le Noir Identity uses an Attack Skill or Counter Skill against an enemy through an Assist Attack, Passive effect, or other means.
- The effect will not activate if the said ally is immobilized/unable to act and cannot use the Skill.

3. The Passive text will be revised to clarify its activation timing and which Skills qualify.
- Before: Before Attack of another "Le Noir" allied Identity on an enemy, this unit uses "Judgment!" Skill as an Unopposed Attack against the main target (once per turn)
- After: Before another "Le Noir" allied Identity uses Attack Skills or Counter Skills on an enemy, this unit uses "Judgment!" Skill as an Unopposed Attack against the main target (once per turn)

We apologize for the confusion caused by these repeated corrections to the Identity's performance and behavior. We recognize that we have failed to reflect the design changes accurately in both the implementation and the text, and failed to catch those errors during review.

Going forward, we will improve communication during development, verify that implementation and text agree, and strengthen our review of individual cases, including Defense Skills, activation timing, and whether a unit is able to act.

We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience.

entry.content:
Announcements

Oct. 15th New Content - Mirror of Sisyphe

October 14, 2026
Identities & E.G.OMirror DungeonEventsNew Content

Greetings, Dear Manager.

The new content Mirror Dungeon 8 「Mirror of Sisyphe」 will be added with the Oct. 15th, 2026 (KST) Scheduled Update.

▶ Date : After 26/10/15 (KST) Scheduled Update

▶ Requirements Normal Difficulty: Clear Main Story Chapter 2 Hard Difficulty: Clear Main Story Chapter 9

▶ How to Activate Hard Mode: From the Theme Pack selection menu, select the "Difficulty Toggle" button to switch between Hard and Normal difficulties

▶ How to enter Parallel Superposition Mode:
Clear 1F ~ 5F with the Parallel Superposition Mode toggled ON

▶ How to enter EXTREME Mode: Clear up to 10F with the Parallel Superposition Mode toggled ON

Notes

1. With the introduction of Mirror Dungeon #8 「Mirror of Sisyphe」, Mirror Dungeon #7 [Mirror of Names and Spiders] will be closed.
※ Theme Pack Compendium recorded from Mirror Dungeon #7 will not be reset.

2. With the Oct. 15th Scheduled Update, Normal, Hard, Parallel Superposition, and EXTREME Modes will be updated simultaneously for 「Mirror of Sisyphe」.

3. 4 new Theme Packs, 8 new E.G.O Gifts, and 6 new Choice Events will be added.

4. Once Mirror of Sisyphe updates, any Starlight acquired in Mirror of Names and Spiders will be removed and will not carry over. A certain amount of starting Starlight will be given by default so that all Managers can start using the Starlight system immediately.

5.26/10/15 (KST) Scheduled Update Maintenance will last from 06:00 ~ 12:00.
Major changes to Mirror Dungeon systems will be deployed after the Scheduled Update. Therefore, with the end of Scheduled Maintenance at 12:00, your Mirror Dungeon Weekly Bonus eligibility and your current Mirror Dungeon run progress will be reset. Rewards for Mirror Dungeon runs that remain incomplete before Oct 15th, 06:00 will become inaccessible with the progress reset, so please claim your rewards BEFORE the Scheduled Update Maintenance begins.

6. 「Mirror of Names and Spiders」 Achievements progress and rewards will become unavailable when 「Mirror of Sisyphe」 is updated.
Please take note of this information to claim your rewards BEFORE the Oct. 15th Scheduled Maintenance.
※ Please note that Mirror Dungeon #8 「Mirror of Sisyphe」 Mirror Projection / Achievements will be updated at a later date.

7. Hidden Bosses featured in the EXTREME Mode will be updated at a later date.
※ Hidden Boss E.G.O Gifts obtainable from Mirror Dungeon #7 EXTREME will have their specs partially adjusted when the Hidden Boss roster is changed at a later date.

Progression

Entering the dungeon, as before, does not cost any resources. However, you can spend Enkephalin modules at the end of your exploration to receive rewards.

<Major Changes>

1. Enemy levels will be raised to Level 65.

2. 4 new Theme Packs and 8 new E.G.O Gifts will be added.
※ This update features 1 new Theme Pack for the Normal
difficulty, 3 new Theme Packs exclusive to the Hard difficulty, and 8 new E.G.O Gifts.

Creating your TEAM

In Normal Difficulty, your Identity Levels will be fixed at
65. In Hard Difficulty, your actual Identity Levels will be reflected.

※ Your current Uptie & E.G.O Threadspinning Tiers will be reflected in the Mirror Dungeon regardless of difficulty, just as they were in the previous Mirror Dungeons.

Grace of the Sisyphean Star

The 「Grace of the Star of Names and Spiders」 will be replaced with 「Grace of the Sisyphean Star」. From 「Grace of the Sisyphean Star」, you can obtain Grace of Stars with special effects by spending Starlight.

Select the "Select All Graces" button to select all graces at once. Select the "+" or "++" buttons below the "Enhance All" button to enhance all graces at once.
※ Please note that choosing either of the "Enhance All" buttons does not select the said graces; either select the "Select All Graces" button or manually select Graces of your choice.

※ If you do not purchase the Grace of Stars, you can obtain the remaining sum of Starlight, either from the Starlight Bonus of your Team or the base sum, as a reward upon clearing the Mirror Dungeon run.

※ Selecting Grace of Stars consumes your starting Starlight & Starlight Bonuses first, and will tap into your Starlight reserve only when you have exceeded that amount.

※ You may not be able to select Grace of Stars if you have insufficient Starlight & Starlight Bonuses.

Starting E.G.O Gifts

Upon entering the Mirror Dungeon, players will be presented with E.G.O Gift Keyword categories to choose from. Starting E.G.O Gifts are fixed for each Keyword, and you can select as many E.G.O Gifts as you are allowed to select within each category. Also, the E.G.O Gift of the Keyword category you select here will appear more frequently during the Mirror Dungeon run.

E.G.O Gift Search

After selecting your Starting E.G.O Gifts, you will be brought to the "E.G.O Gift Search" screen, where you can obtain up to 3 additional E.G.O Gifts (Tier 3 or below) of your choice. Each E.G.O Gift selection will increase the price of the next choice.

※ E.G.O Gift Search becomes available only when the "Activate Gift Search" option is toggled ON in your Starting E.G.O Gift selection menu.

Selecting Theme Packs

Select a Dungeon Theme to explore upon entering a new floor. Choose a Theme Pack by selecting the pack of your choice and dragging it downward.

Select the difficulty switch button at the top-right part of the screen to toggle between Normal and Hard difficulties. Certain Theme Packs featured in the Hard difficulty pose a significantly higher difficulty compared to those found in the Normal difficulty. Hard Difficulty shows a total of 4 E.G.O Gift Clear Bonuses.
※ Once Hard difficulty has been toggled on, you cannot switch back to Normal difficulty.

<Major Changes>

1. 4 new Theme Packs and 8 new E.G.O Gifts will be added.
※ This update features 1 new Theme Pack for the Normal difficulty, 3 new Theme Packs exclusive to the Hard difficulty, and 8 new E.G.O Gifts.

2. The new Theme Packs will add a total of 6 new Choice Events.
New E.G.O Gifts can be obtained from the said Choice Events.

Theme Pack Search

This is the "Theme Pack Search" function, accessible by pressing the "Search" button. Using this function, you can spend Starlight to search for and select a Theme Pack of your choice. However, please note that the selectable Theme Pack pool is limited to what is available from your current Floor and Difficulty.

※ Theme Pack Observation fee rises with every use.

※ Searching for and selecting a new, previously unaccessed Theme Pack costs 50% more Starlight.

Encounters

After selecting the Theme Pack of your choice, select a Stage node to begin Combat Encounters or Choice Events.

In the Hard difficulty, only up to 2 nodes from the current position can be viewed.

Shops

You can spend your Cost at the Shops to purchase E.G.O Gifts or use one of its many useful services for progressing through the Mirror Dungeon.

There is a chance for Super Shops to appear in Hard Difficulty Theme Packs. The more Cost you spend in a Shop, the greater the chance for a Super Shop to spawn on the next Floor.

The following are the benefits provided by Super Shops.
- E.G.O Gift Shop Selection +3
- Skill Replacement Opportunity +1 (cannot replace the Skill of the same Identity again)
- Access to "ID Skill Search" option, which lets you choose which Identity's Skills you want to replace
- Can fuse up to 5 E.G.O Gifts at once in Fusion
- Greater chance for higher Tier E.G.O Gifts to appear when Fusing (Fusion Point Modifier)

Replacing Skills

You can spend a certain amount of Cost to replace the Skills of Identities in your loadout. However, if you have completely removed a Skill in favor of another in previous Shops, that Skill can no longer be replaced.

※ In "Super Shops" that may spawn in Hard Difficulty, Skill Replacement for 2 Identities will now be shown at once instead of appearing one after another. Also, "Identity Skill Search," a new function to pick and choose which Identity's Skill you would like to replace, will become available.

3★ Skill Replacement can only replace Skills within the same Identity, even when using the ID Skill Search function.

※ Using ID Skill Search to replace Skills is more expensive than standard Skill Replacement.

※ ID Skill Search cost is fixed, and is not affected by modifiers from Grace of Stars or E.G.O Gifts.

Wishmaking

Through "Wishmaking," you can spend Starlight to improve your Fusion chances.

※ Each instance of Wishmaking uses the same amount of Starlight regardless of how many times it has been activated.

※ Depending on the number of E.G.O Gifts used, the forecast maxes out at 99.99%.

Encounter Reward Cards

Each Encounter has a certain chance to provide you with a selection of "Encounter Reward Cards". Higher-difficulty Mirror Dungeons, higher Floors, and higher-difficulty Encounters will yield higher-value rewards.

Trials upon each Floor Completion

Clear the Floor to gain an E.G.O Gift of your choice. Selecting an E.G.O Gift will give you its linked "Mounting Trials" and Enemy level-up effects.

You can select 2 Reward E.G.O Gifts upon clearing a Hard Difficulty Theme Pack. However, please note that you will gain 2 Mounting Trials linked to each E.G.O Gift as well.

※ Should you refuse to select any E.G.O Gifts by selecting the "Refuse Gift" button, a number of the given Mounting Trials will be randomly selected.

Parallel Superposition & EXTREME Modes

Clearing IF ~ 5F of the Mirror Dungeon on Hard difficulty unlocks access to Mirror Dungeon Parallel Superposition & EXTREME Modes, which present an even higher level of challenge. In Mirror of Sisyphe, Parallel Superposition lasts from 6F ~ 10F, and EXTREME from 11F ~ 15F, presenting even further empowered enemies.

The combination of Mounting Trials and Adversities in Mirror of Sisyphe EXTREME mode will greatly empower the enemies; the higher your Floor, the more Starlight and Projection you will obtain.

※ Please note that Parallel Superposition and EXTREME modes present a high level of difficulty and exist for purposes of challenge runs or for clearing Achievements, which will be added with a future update.

EXTREME Mode - Adversities

- For Parallel Superposition EXTREME, in addition to Mounting Trials applicable when entering Floor 11, you will have an option to set "Adversities" for yourself.

- Starting from Floor 11, up to 6 Adversities can be selected on each Floor. Just like Mounting Trials, Adversities will continue to compound instead of going away.

- Selecting more Adversities will net more Adversity rewards; you will gain additional Starlight based on your cumulative Adversity Score.

※ Adversities aren't mandatory; you can reach Floor 15 without setting any Adversities, which may still be a good strategy to experience the dungeon.

※ Mirror of Sisyphe Projection Levels can be updated only after the Mirror Projection / Achievement update, which will arrive at a later date.

Exploration Complete and Starlight Reward

Upon completion, you can view your statistics and progress of the relevant Mirror Dungeon run.

※ Starlight Rewards The following are ways to increase the amount of Starlight gained upon clearing a Mirror Dungeon run.

- Clearing at higher Floors gives more Starlight.
- Clearing in Hard difficulty gives more Starlight.
- Clearing Refraction Railway Theme Pack gives more Starlight.
- Select Starlight Encounter Reward Cards to gain additional Starlight.
- Higher Starlight Bonus in the Team loadout window gives a better Starlight multiplier.

<Major Changes>

1. Any Starlight acquired in Mirror Dungeon #7 will be removed and will not carry over.
A certain amount of starting Starlight will be given by default so that all Managers can start using the Starlight system immediately.

[Other Sources of Starlight]

Starlight, which is a Mirror Dungeon resource, can be obtained via Extractions and Yisang Exchanges as well.

※ Other sources of Starlight (There is a single, first-time opportunity to gain Starlight from one of the following conditions):

- Obtain a newly released 3★ Identity or E.G.O from New Target Extractions.
- Within a certain period of time, obtain a newly released 3★ Identity or E.G.O from Extractions.
- Within a certain period of time, obtain a newly released 3★ Identity or E.G.O from Yisang Exchange.
- Within a certain period of time, obtain a newly released 3★ Identity or E.G.O from Extraction or Yisang Exchange after obtaining it from the Dispenser.

※ What are not Starlight acquisition conditions:
- Obtaining a newly released Identity or E.G.O from the Dispenser.
- Extracting the same newly released Identity or E.G.O for the second time or obtaining it from Yisang Exchange for the second time or more.
- Obtaining the said Identity or E.G.O outside the certain period of time.

[Weekly Bonuses]

Mirror Dungeon Hard Difficulty with Weekly Bonuses yields more Battle Pass EXP compared to Mirror Dungeon Normal. Your reward will be based on the number of Floors you cleared and the Difficulties you selected for each Floor.

※ However, without Weekly Bonuses, the clear reward between Hard and Normal is identical, just as it had been in the previous Mirror Dungeons.

If you have selected the Hard Difficulty for every floor, you can use two or more Weekly Bonuses at once. The maximum obtainable Reward per week is identical to the amount obtained from clearing Mirror Dungeon #7 (Mirror of Names and Spiders) Hard Difficulty Floor 5.

- Using 3 Weekly Bonuses all at once: Lunacy x750, Battle Pass EXP x225
- Using 3 Weekly Bonuses 3 times, one at a time: Lunacy x750, Battle Pass EXP 250

Upon clearing the Mirror Dungeon, based on the number of Theme Packs cleared in the Hard Difficulty, your Starlight reward will be greatly increased. Also, clearing Refraction Railway Theme Packs, which are exclusive to Hard Difficulty runs, will each yield bonus Starlight as well.

※ While Weekly Bonuses can be used for runs cleared before reaching 5F, please note that your Weekly Bonus will be reduced based on the number of floors you did not clear.

E.G.O Gifts

<Major Changes>

1. 8 new E.G.O Gifts will be added.

※ 2 new E.G.O Gifts are obtainable from both Normal and Hard, and 6 new E.G.O Gifts are exclusive to the Hard Difficulty.

2. Keywords of certain E.G.O Gifts will be adjusted.
→ Relevant E.G.O Gifts: Universal Instinct, Universal Skeleton
- Before: They were categorized as Keywordless Gifts
- After: They are now Bleed Gifts

3. Theme Pack availability for a certain E.G.O Gift will be adjusted.
→ Relevant E.G.O Gift: WB Flask
- Before: Featured in all Theme Packs
- After: La Manchaland Re-opening, The Infinite Procession, The Dream Ending, Who Couldn't be Bloodfiends, Blessed Carnival, and The Master of La Manchaland

4. The E.G.O Gift "Blue Starshard" has been identified as having unintentional effects, so its description will be adjusted.
→ Relevant Effect: - When dealing damage against the affected enemies with Skills that apply Sinking, Sinking Count, or Unique Sinking, inflict X Defense Level Down (Y times per turn)
- Before: This effect inflicts Defense Level Down next turn.
- Updated the description with "inflict X Defense Level Down next turn" to match its behavior

5. The E.G.O Gift "Searing Brass" description will be updated.
- Before: When an enemy takes Burn damage, deal Wrath damage equal to Burn Potency
- After: When an enemy takes Burn damage due to Burn activation, deal Wrath damage equal to Burn Potency

<Major Changes>

6. Certain E.G.O Gift effects not working as intended will be fixed.

(1) Dimensional Perception Modifier
- Before: The "Discard" effect trigger checked for Discards activated by E.G.O Gifts as well
- After: Fixed the E.G.O Gift behavior so that it does not trigger for Discards activated by E.G.O Gifts

(2) Purloined Flame
→ Relevant Effects On Hit with a Skill(including E.G.O Skills): if the target has 3+ Burn Count, activate Burn once on the target. (target loses 1 Burn Count; activates once per Skill) Turn End: targets with 3+ Burn Count activate Burn one more time (target loses 1 Burn Count)
- Before: Instead of activating Burn, it was "dealing damage equal to Burn Potency."
- After: This effect now activates Burn, as described

(3) Charge-type Gloves Keyword "Near-light Superbattery"
→ Relevant Effect: When this unit consumes Charge Count with its Skills, consume the same amount of Charge Count 1 more time (when there isn't enough Charge Count, consume as much as available)
- Before: This effect consumed more Charge Count than the actual number of Charge Count available on the affected unit
- After: This effect now consumes as much Charge Count as available, as described

(4) Torn Bandolier
→ Relevant Effect 1: Pierce Skills gain Clash Power +1
- Before: This effect activated only on Pierce Base Attack Skills
- After: Now, this effect activates for all Pierce Attack Skills, as described
→ Skills that consume Ammo deal +(X/# of Coins)% damage
- Before: When an Identity that does not have Ammo used an E.G.O Skill that spends Ammo, this E.G.O Gift effect did not trigger
- After: This E.G.O Gift effect now triggers for E.G.O Skills that gain/spend Ammo

※ More E.G.O Gift adjustments are planned for the future.

※ Future E.G.O Gift adjustment details will be shared in notices for each respective adjustment update.
